newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Basic to issue over-the-counter ADRs.
newsitem.headline: Basic to issue over-the-counter ADRs.

text.p: Philippine oil explorer Basic Petroleum & Minerals Corp said on Friday it would launch over-the-counter American Depositary Receipts (ADR) within three to six months' time.
Basic senior executive vice president Ramon Mayuga told Reuters it had assigned Bank of New York Co Inc as the issuer of the ADRs.
One ADR will be comprised of 2,000 Basic shares.
"We expect the programme to be fully operational within three to six months," Mayuga said.
The ADRs will be priced according to the value of the local shares. Basic shares were last traded on September 19 and closed at 0.95 centavos.
The United States' Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) recently approved its application for a Level 1 Depositary Receipt programme, the company said.
The company said it will undertake a roadshow in the U.S. to introduce the company to American investors.
Before the launching, a correspondent local bank would buy Basic shares from the local market and put them into custody. These shares will be the underlying issues for the ADRs.
Mayuga said the number of Basic shares to be bought will depend on the interest generated from U.S. investors.
The programme will not generate new money, but will give an additional instrument for the American investors.
"It will be more cost efficient for them (American investors) to invest in Basic shares in their own home country. They will overcome forex restrictions and forex risk," Mayuga added.
"This is just an entry level. Hopefully, we can do some fund-raising down the line," he said.
Basic recently announced it would diversify into real estate but has not yet detailed its plans.
